investigation.claim: A HEAD response has no response content in the worldwide HTTP standard published in June 2022.

assertion.text: A HEAD response has no response content in the worldwide HTTP standard published in June 2022.

analysis.reason: Direct factual verification of HTTP standard specification regarding HEAD response content.

components.text: A HEAD response has no response content
components.subject: A HEAD response

result.scope_note: Verified against RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics) published June 2022, which explicitly states that a HEAD response MUST NOT include a message body and any Content-Length field MUST be omitted or set to zero.

explanation.text: A HEAD response has no response content (message body) according to RFC 9110 §9.3.2 and RFC 9112 §6.3, which both state the server MUST NOT send content in the response.
The worldwide HTTP standard published in June 2022 includes RFC 9110, RFC 9111, and RFC 9112, all released in June 2022, as confirmed by RFC identification and publication metadata.
RFC 9110 §9.3.2 explicitly states: 'The HEAD method is identical to GET except that the server MUST NOT send content in the response.'

1. Any response to a HEAD request and any response with a [1xx (Informational)](rfc9110.html#status.1xx), [204 (No Content)](rfc9110.html#status.204), or [304 (Not Modified)](rfc9110.html#status.304) status code is always terminated by the first empty line after the header fields, regardless of the header fields present in the message, and thus cannot contain a message body or trailer section.

excerpts.text: Since June 2022 it has been defined by RFC 9112 (the HTTP/1.1 message syntax), RFC 9110 (the semantics every HTTP version shares) and RFC 9111 (caching), which together replaced RFC 7230 to RFC 7235.

* HTTP/1.1 is now specified across three documents published in June 2022: RFC 9110 "HTTP Semantics" (STD 97), RFC 9111 "HTTP Caching" (STD 98) and RFC 9112 "HTTP/1.1" (STD 99). RFC 9110 obsoletes RFC 2818 and RFC 7230 to 7235 (except 7234), RFC 9111 obsoletes RFC 7234, and RFC 9112 obsoletes the message syntax parts of RFC 7230.
